# Susan Baker

## Overview

- **Age:** Elderly  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005)</sub>

- **Role:** Maid-of-all-work and housekeeper  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Susan Baker  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000)</sub>

## Appearance

Susan is a grim-faced, gray, and gaunt elderly woman. She acknowledges that she is no beauty, though she feels sensitive when portrayed as uglier than she considers herself.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005), [v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000), [v5 c17 P33](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0033), [v5 c30 P14](../source/v05-c30.md#nw-v05-c30-p0014)_

## Personality

Susan is a practical, kind-hearted, and faithful woman who reigns supreme over the household duties at Ingleside. She maintains an optimistic and serene approach to life, leaving humanity's betterment to Higher Powers rather than worrying about running the world. Unmarried and straightforward, she is candid about liking men and unsentimental about romance or poetry, which she considers mostly lies. She takes pride in her domestic skills, especially her cooking, and enjoys discussing topics like funerals.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c19 P41](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0041), [v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005), [v4 c40 P49](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0049), [v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000), [v5 c1 P7](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0007), [v5 c15 P3](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0003), [v5 c16 P8](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0008), [v5 c26 P8](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0008), [v5 c26 P9](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0009)_

## History

Susan was installed as the maid-of-all-work for Gilbert and Anne Blythe while they lived at the little house at Four Winds. Gilbert insisted that she be kept on, and she quickly took full charge of the household duties and pantry. During her time there, she briefly left to tend to her sister Matilda, who had broken her leg. When the Blythe family moved to Ingleside, Susan relocated with them, taking charge of the household where she remained the central authority over domestic matters. She cared for the Blythe children with great devotion, taking Shirley to her brother's home for three months during his parents' absence and looking after Walter when he suffered from a toothache.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c22 P0](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0000), [v4 c22 P3](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0003), [v4 c36 P19](../source/v04-c36.md#nw-v04-c36-p0019), [v4 c36 P21](../source/v04-c36.md#nw-v04-c36-p0021), [v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000), [v5 c1 P7](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0007), [v5 c16 P8](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0008)_

## Quotes

> You just take it easy, Mrs. Doctor, dear. Have a good time and do not worry about the pantry. Susan is at the helm. There is no use in keeping a dog and doing your own barking. I am going to take your breakfast up to you every morning.  <sub>[v4 c22 P3](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0003)</sub>

> I am an old maid, but you never hear ME abusing the men. I like ’em. I would have married one if I could.  <sub>[v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005)</sub>

> Well, I never was much hand for weeping, Mrs. Doctor, dear. I would rather fall to and cheer people up than weep with them.  <sub>[v4 c40 P49](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0049)</sub>

> Starving and beating a child, Mrs. Dr. dear! As you know, I hold with lawful spanking, but I go no further.  <sub>[v5 c8 P9](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0009)</sub>

> Cornelia Elliott thinks she was born to run this world, Mrs. Dr. dear, and so she is always in a stew over something. I have never thought I was, and so I go calmly along.  <sub>[v5 c26 P9](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0009)</sub>
